title: Optimize Dictionary `get` and `get_or_add`
body:

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Micro-optimize `Dictionary` `get` and `get_or_add`.

## Additional information

`Dictionary::get` and `Dictionary::get_or_add` both call `Dictionary::getptr` which performs an additional redundant type check/conversion. This can be expensive for script typed Dictionaries with long inheritance chains.

## Benchmarks

<details>
<summary>Testing code</summary>

Put in `tests/core/test_containers.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "tests/test_macros.h"

TEST_FORCE_LINK(test_containers)

#include <chrono>
#include <cstdio>
#include "core/object/ref_counted.h"

class CustomObject : public RefCounted {
	GDCLASS(CustomObject, RefCounted);
};

const int SCENARIOS = 4;

namespace DictionaryTests {
void setup(Dictionary &d, Variant &v, int scenario) {
	switch(scenario) {
		// int, untyped
		case 0:
			v = 1;
			break;
		// object (refcounted), untyped
		case 1:
			v = memnew(CustomObject);
			break;
		// int, mismatch
		case 2:
			v = 1.1;
			d.set_typed(Variant::INT, StringName(), Variant(), Variant::INT, StringName(), Variant());
			break;
		// object (refcounted), typed
		case 3:
			v = memnew(CustomObject);
			d.set_typed(Variant::OBJECT, v.operator Object *()->get_class_name(), v.operator Object *()->get_script(), Variant::INT, StringName(), Variant());
			break;
	}
}

__attribute__((optimize("O0")))
double getptr(int scenario) {
	Dictionary d;
	Variant v;
	setup(d, v, scenario);
	const int N = 100'000'000;

	auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

	for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
		const Variant *x = d.getptr(v);
	}

	double ret = std::chrono::duration<double, std::nano>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start).count() / N;

	printf("%.2lf\n", ret);
	fflush(stdout);

	return ret;
}

__attribute__((optimize("O0")))
double get(int scenario) {
	Dictionary d;
	Variant v;
	setup(d, v, scenario);
	Variant w(0);
	const int N = 100'000'000;

	auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

	for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
		d.get(v, w);
	}

	double ret = std::chrono::duration<double, std::nano>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start).count() / N;

	printf("%.2lf\n", ret);
	fflush(stdout);

	return ret;
}

double get_or_add(int scenario) {
	Dictionary d;
	Variant v;
	Variant w(0);
	setup(d, v, scenario);
	const int N = 100'000'000;

	auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

	for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
		d.get_or_add(v, w);
	}

	double ret = std::chrono::duration<double, std::nano>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start).count() / N;

	printf("%.2lf\n", ret);
	fflush(stdout);

	return ret;
}

}

static void containers() {
	// Times to run each test.
	const int N = 3;

	LocalVector<double> data[SCENARIOS][N];

#define run_loop(test) printf(#test"\n");\
	for (int n = 0; n < N; n++) {\
		data[s][n].push_back(test(s));\
	}\

	for (int s = 0; s < SCENARIOS; s++) {
		printf("SCENARIO %c\n", 'A' + s);
		puts("=====");
		run_loop(DictionaryTests::getptr);
		run_loop(DictionaryTests::get);
		run_loop(DictionaryTests::get_or_add);

		printf("\n\n");
	}

	// Print csv-like output
	for (int s = 0; s < SCENARIOS; s++) {
		printf("SCENARIO %c\n", 'A' + s);

		for (unsigned int n = 0; n < N; n++) {
			for (unsigned int i = 0; i < data[s][n].size(); i++) {
				printf("%.2lf%c", data[s][n][i], i == data[s][n].size() - 1 ? '\n' : ',');
			}
		}
	}
	fflush(stdout);
}

REGISTER_TEST_COMMAND("containers", &containers)
```

Run with `./bin/godot...exe --test containers`
</details>

<details>
<summary>Specs and test setup</summary>
CPU: AMD 9800X3D, GPU: AMD RX 6800, RAM: 32GB 6400 CL28

Windows 11, Release templates built with GCC (MinGW)

Each run of the test runs each function loop 3x on all scenarios. Both versions were run 6 times and the 18 results were aggregated by 20th percentile. `N=100_000_000`.
</details>

`getptr` performance should not change but is left in results for comparison. `A`, `B` and `C` should see near no difference since we only save one comparison. Scenario `D` is where the expensive checks show up.
### A: Int untyped

| Function | Master (ns/op) | PR (ns/op) | Diff | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `getptr` | 1.28 | 1.28 | 0 | 1x |
| `get` | 2.51 | 2.45 | -0.06 | 1.02x |
| `get_or_add` | 6.82 | 6.17 | -0.65 | 1.1x |

### B: RefCounted untyped

| Function | Master (ns/op) | PR (ns/op) | Diff | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `getptr` | 1.28 | 1.28 | 0 | 1x |
| `get` | 2.49 | 2.44 | -0.05 | 1.02x |
| `get_or_add` | 14.47 | 14.61 | +0.15 | 0.99x |

### C: Int typed (Float conversion)

| Function | Master (ns/op) | PR (ns/op) | Diff | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `getptr` | 8.27 | 8.27 | 0 | 1x |
| `get` | 9.53 | 9.44 | -0.09 | 1.01x |
| `get_or_add` | 13.34 | 12.55 | -0.79 | 1.06x |

### D: RefCounted typed

| Function | Master (ns/op) | PR (ns/op) | Diff | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `getptr` | 3.85 | 3.85 | 0 | 1x |
| `get` | 7.70 | 5.01 | -2.69 | 1.54x |
| `get_or_add` | 17.70 | 16.16 | -1.54 | 1.10x |
